newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin feels well, but tired by paperwork - doctor.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin feels well, but tired by paperwork - doctor.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin is cheerful and feeling moderately well at the Gorky-9 residence outside Moscow, but he is tired from working on documents, chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov told a television interview.

"He feels quite well, rather cheerful, even though of course he is tired from quite a long stint working on documents," Mironov told the MSNBC network in an interview. Mironov said he had just seen Yeltsin.
Yeltsin, who turns 66 on February 1, moved to Gorky-9 on Monday after 12 days of treatment for pneumonia in Moscow's Central Clinical Hospital.
Mironov said Yeltsin's doctors had found no medical reasons to suggest the president could not continue running Russia. He said Yeltsin had worked on documents for about eight hours on Tuesday.
"Today all day starting from early morning for about eight hours Boris Nikolayevich (Yeltsin) worked on documents which had accumulated recently -- there were some telephone calls," he said.
Yeltsin underwent heart bypass surgery on November 5, but doctors have said there was no link between the heart operation and the pneumonia.
